narrative:
The decision regarding your law school application was influenced by a prediction that you have a 64% chance of failing the bar exam on your first attempt. This high probability indicates significant concerns about your readiness for the challenges of legal practice, which ultimately led to the rejection of your application.

The most influential factor in this prediction was your choice to work part-time while studying. This situation can create additional stress and time constraints, which may hinder your ability to fully engage with your studies. In contrast, the majority of accepted students are able to commit to full-time study, allowing them to focus entirely on their academic performance.

Your performance in your first year of studies also played a role. You are currently in a lower decile compared to the average of accepted students, suggesting that your grades may not reflect the level of understanding and mastery needed for success in law school and on the bar exam. While your third-year grades are better, they still do not fully offset the concerns raised by your earlier performance.

Lastly, your undergraduate GPA is slightly below the average of accepted students, which further contributes to the model's prediction. This GPA, combined with your other factors, suggests that you may not have demonstrated the academic rigor typically associated with successful bar exam candidates.

Moving forward, consider focusing on improving your academic performance and exploring options that allow you to dedicate more time to your studies. Engaging in preparatory courses or seeking academic support could also enhance your readiness for future applications.
